Ticket 302 slice 1 (2026-09-09): the composed-host boot defect was fixed at the root — WindowsEventLogAvailabilityHealthCheck took IWindowsEventLogSink as a REQUIRED dependency while ResilientWindowsEventLogRegistration.Add registers that sink on Windows only, so every /health request on macOS threw inside the health middleware and answered 500. Eleven of the seventeen rows burned down with that one fix and were removed here.
The four environmental rows are OS gaps, not defects: each names the platform facility macOS lacks. The two NPrincipal rows are a DEFECT and need a follow-up ticket; they are not an OS gap.

Ticket 360 (2026-09-13): the two behavioural NPrincipalAcceptance rows are REMOVED, not re-dated. They were never an OS gap: InstallationFounderBootstrapCeremony built only the DesktopOsSession claim issuer, which declines when Environment.UserInteractive is false -- every Windows service and every launchd daemon -- so a headless node could not issue a founder bootstrap claim at all and the attach returned Unavailable. The ceremony now falls back to the SelfHostedFileSystemOwner issuer that BootstrapClaimRedemption.IsAccepted already admitted. A permitted behavioural failure is a defect nobody has to fix; that is why this one survived weeks and also kept winbox out of the gate. Environmental rows name a facility the platform lacks; behavioural rows do not belong in this list.

Ticket 360 (2026-09-13), superseding the entry above: the two NPrincipalAcceptance rows RETURN, with a narrower and measured reason. The previous entry removed them on the premise that the headless-bootstrap fix resolved both. It resolved one. The TRX 360 slice 1 landed retention for -- used here for the first time -- shows macOS failing with no_response while Windows failed with Unavailable: two defects, not one. The headless fix is real and proven; the macOS no_response is not fixed and is out of scope for 360. These rows are permitted ONLY on macOS: Windows now permits nothing, which is strictly narrower than the list this ticket inherited.

Ticket 435 (2026-09-15): the two W4 rows are GONE from permittedFailures because they now pass. LocalNodeLanTransport asked for X509KeyStorageFlags.EphemeralKeySet unconditionally and macOS has never supported it, so the node leaf could not load and the LAN listener never bound. Choosing the flags per platform fixed both. verify-macos on PR 139 (run 34914670228) reported them as burn-down rows -- the gate refuses a baseline that permits a test which no longer fails, which is how this was measured rather than assumed. Four permitted failures remain: the Windows Event Log sink (a real macOS gap), the keystore ownership assertion (ticket 434), and the two NPrincipal rows (ticket 360).

permittedFailures.reason: PlatformNotSupportedException: 'Mac keychain integration scheduled for Wave 2 mobile / desktop packaging.' The in-process runtime cannot start on macOS because the install keystore is DPAPI/keychain-bound; the Windows Event Log the test injects has no macOS counterpart either.
Keystore and data-directory ownership are per-platform (Windows ACLs and .dpapi keys versus POSIX modes); the assertion names the Windows shape.

Ticket 360 (2026-09-13): the retained TRX gives this failure verbatim as {"error":"no_response"}. That is NOT the headless-bootstrap defect 360 fixed -- that one failed with 'founder attach status: Unavailable' and is now gone on BOTH platforms (winbox reports failed 0; the headless filesystem-owner claim test passes here too). 360 was two defects sharing one symptom list. This row is the second one, still open, and it is macOS-only: the same E2E case passes on Windows, so it is a behavioural defect on this platform, not an OS gap. The follow-up ticket is T-423, which owns these two rows: it fixes the no_response or proves it an OS gap and reclassifies them, and removes them from this file in the same PR as its fix.
